summary: Ran the molecular tests for M1-S03 (build tier2-webhook, type automation, owner apex-builder, status entering this run: built). Two always-on checks plus the step's three declared checkers all passed: 12/12 *-meta.xml files parse at apiVersion 67.0, both triggers declare 'after update'; the manifest check is skipped-not-applicable under the Apex exception (apex-builder ships no package.xml; M1-S05 aggregates); check_apex_queueable_patterns.py, check_callouts_and_http_integrations.py --fail-on HIGH and check_platform_events_apex.py each exited 0 with zero findings at any severity, matching the owning agent's own reported results. check-outputs confirmed all 20 declared outputs present, non-empty and well-formed (exit 0). A mechanical brace/paren/bracket/string-balance scan (comments and string literals stripped) over all 12 Apex files found no mismatch. The one declared manual test is classified usable (two independently observable outcomes) and deferred to the M1 gate, with one inline caveat: its clause (b) still names templates/apex/HttpClient.cls, a template remedy B dropped from this build. results.json was written with passed: true, failed: [], and the step was transitioned built -> tested via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Per this agent's Step 7 override: every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly (no test was refused, no checker was missing, no manifest exclusion had to be applied for a coverage-gap type -- the manifest skip is the documented Apex exception, not a coverage-gap exclusion).

process_observations.observation: Every declared checker exited 0 with zero findings at any severity, not merely zero blocking findings, matching exactly what the owning agent's own envelope reported for the same commands.

check-outputs confirmed all 20 declared outputs present, non-empty, and (for the meta XML among them) parseable, and a mechanical brace/paren/bracket/string-balance scan over all 12 Apex files with comments and strings stripped found no mismatch -- the cheapest structural checks this loop can run with no target org, and both came back clean.

The build-level P1 finding from the owning agent's run 2 stands unresolved: remedy B dropped templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls (-> TriggerControl -> Trigger_Setting__mdt), so this build ships CaseTrigger with no admin kill switch and no data-load bypass -- a bulk Case-ownership reassignment into Tier_2_Engineering will escalate every affected Case.

Tier2_Escalation__e.Severity__c is mapped from Case.Priority with no clarification saying it should be; the assignment carries an inline // UNVERIFIED comment in the shipped code. Not adjudicated here -- recorded so it is not lost between tested and the milestone gate.

Two library documents disagree about Test.setMock ordering: skills/apex/apex-named-credentials-patterns/references/code-examples.md section 6 places setMock before Test.startTest, while the declared checker check_callouts_and_http_integrations.py (rule 6, run this step at --fail-on HIGH) flags exactly that ordering as HIGH, matching the ordering skills/apex/test-class-standards/references/code-examples.md uses. This step's test classes follow the checker's ordering and the checker exited 0 -- the step's artefacts are not at fault, but the contradiction between the two skill documents is unresolved and this agent does not adjudicate which skill is wrong.

The manual acceptance test's own clause (b) names templates/apex/HttpClient.cls as the endpoint-composition path; the shipped code does not use it (Tier2WebhookQueueable.cls line 25 records that remedy B dropped it, and line 220 composes the endpoint directly). The substantive security property clause (b) is checking for -- no literal hostname, no Apex-set X-API-Key/Authorization header -- is satisfied by inspection; the named mechanism in the test's own text is stale.

evidence.path: plan.json steps[M1-S03].acceptance_tests[] (manual, clause b) vs artefacts/M1-S03/classes/Tier2WebhookQueueable.cls lines 25 and 220

process_observations.observation: The step's own acceptance-test description for the callouts checker says it fails on 'a test with setMock after startTest', which is the opposite of what the checker's code enforces (it fails on setMock with no preceding startTest). Already recorded by the owning agent and the runner in prior envelopes; repeated here only because a reader debugging a future failure from PLAN.md's prose alone would be sent the wrong way.

Nothing in the build's 45 clarifications says whether the org already has an after-update trigger on Case; this step ships CaseTrigger assuming none exists. If one does, deploying a second after-update trigger on Case will not simply add alongside it.
The step is now tested; PLAN.md, decisions.md and traceability.md have not yet absorbed the P1 kill-switch loss, the Severity mapping question, or the manifest Apex-exception note.
